name: Amphetamine / Adderall
lead: Adderall is a prescription mixed-salts amphetamine product containing roughly equal parts of amphetamine aspartate, amphetamine sulfate, dextroamphetamine saccharate and dextroamphetamine sulfate, used mainly for ADHD and narcolepsy [2][3]. It is a controlled substance, Schedule II in the US and Class B in the UK [3].

Loss of appetite and weight loss are common effects, and the drug is listed among appetite suppressants [3]. On looksmax.org, users discuss it for focus, appetite control, social disinhibition and gym use, and the forum also discusses obtaining it without a prescription [4][5]. No published trial has tested Adderall as a weight-loss or appearance treatment in healthy people.
Documented risks include cardiovascular effects, insomnia, anxiety, psychosis at heavy use, and addiction; surveys show non-medical use is common among US college students [6][7].

paras: Adderall is approved for ADHD and narcolepsy. Reviews describe long-term stimulant treatment as effective for core ADHD symptoms [3], and controlled trials of mixed amphetamine salts have been run in adults and children with ADHD [8][9]. Reference sources report that low doses can modestly improve cognition in healthy adults while higher doses impair cognitive control, and that stimulants may modestly increase strength and endurance; several sports bodies ban the drug [3].

Reduced appetite and weight loss are common adverse effects, and the FDA advises monitoring height and weight in children and adolescents because of possible reversible growth impairment [3]. Use specifically for weight loss in healthy people is off-label and not supported by dedicated trials.

Physical effects include changes in blood pressure and heart rate, dry mouth, Raynaud's phenomenon and sexual side effects; large doses can cause rhabdomyolysis and dangerous body temperature rises [3]. FDA-commissioned studies in 2011 found no link between therapeutic use and serious cardiovascular events, but use is contraindicated in existing cardiovascular disease [3]. Psychological effects include insomnia, mood swings and anxiety, with psychosis mainly at heavy use [3].

Reference sources describe a high potential for misuse. Recreational doses are far larger than therapeutic ones, tolerance develops quickly, and withdrawal is common in heavy users [3]. A national survey of 10,904 US college students examined non-medical use of prescription stimulants including Adderall, and a second survey of 4,580 students examined motives and routes of administration [6][7]. Studies have also mined Twitter for non-medical Adderall use [10].

Forum threads include users asking about first-time use for study, others describing experiences, and posts about the stimulant's effect on social inhibition, appetite and the gym [4][5]. Some users warn that pills sold without a prescription are often not Adderall; one reply to a first-time user claims such 30 mg pills are usually pressed methamphetamine, and another reply says an unprescribed purchase is likely meth [4][5]. Public health sources do not verify these specific claims, but the forum posts document the concern in the community.
No studies have tested Adderall for weight loss or appearance goals in healthy people.

ADHD trials exist: a 7-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study of mixed amphetamine salts in 27 adults with ADHD [8], a randomized placebo-controlled study of Adderall XR in children [9], and a comparison of Ritalin and Adderall in children [11]. Registered trials have also examined mixed amphetamine salts for cocaine dependence [12][13]. A rat study reported that amphetamine reduces impulsive decision making and examined the dopaminergic and noradrenergic basis [14].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org Adderall is discussed as a focus drug, appetite suppressant and social enhancer, alongside questions about how to obtain it [4][5].

claims.claim: Prescription ADHD stimulants can be used as an appetite suppressant to lose weight.
claims.believers: Forum posters describe using stimulants to cut appetite while studying or training, and threads discuss how to get a prescription [4].
claims.experts: Appetite loss and weight loss are recognised adverse effects, and the FDA advises growth monitoring in children [3]. No trial has tested the drug as a weight-loss therapy in healthy adults, and it is a controlled drug with abuse potential [3][6].

claims.claim: Adderall from an unprescribed source is often really methamphetamine.
claims.believers: Replies to users asking about unprescribed purchases state that common 30 mg pills are pressed methamphetamine and that such sources are likely not Adderall [4][5].
claims.experts: Reference sources say amphetamine misuse is common among students and describe non-medical use patterns, but do not quantify counterfeit composition [3][6][7].

claims.claim: Stimulants improve social ease and gym performance.
claims.believers: Forum threads describe the drug as a social drug and ask about gym use [4][5].
claims.experts: A 2015 meta-analysis summarised in reference sources found modest cognitive gains at low doses in healthy adults and possible small increases in strength and endurance, while higher doses impair cognitive control [3].

card.summary: A controlled stimulant that suppresses appetite as a side effect; nothing tested for weight loss or looks.
card.aka: Adderall, Adderall XR, mixed amphetamine salts
card.note: Schedule II controlled drug with abuse, cardiovascular and psychiatric risks; unprescribed pills may not be what they claim.

quick.overview:
Adderall is a prescription mixed amphetamine product for ADHD and narcolepsy. Reduced appetite and weight loss are common effects, so some looksmaxxing forum users discuss it for appetite control as well as focus.

No trial has tested it for weight loss in healthy people, and it is a tightly controlled drug in most countries.
quick.mechanism: Amphetamines raise dopamine and norepinephrine signalling by promoting release of these neurotransmitters. Dextroamphetamine is the more potent stimulant component of the mixture.
quick.risks: Documented effects include higher heart rate and blood pressure, insomnia, anxiety, psychosis at heavy use, and dependence with withdrawal. It is Schedule II in the US, Class B in the UK and Schedule I in Canada. Forum users themselves warn that unprescribed pills may be other substances.
